description:
Purpose: confirm quote estimates on the carriers' own quote sites, via Foresee agents completing their real quote flows.

        IDEMPOTENT, keyed on the profile: the first call commissions the
        walks; calling again with the same profile collects progress and
        results instead of re-submitting anything — whatever the ask. A
        profile that has already been walked returns those results (the
        carriers are never asked twice): the envelope's
        ``coverage_selection`` names the ask the walk typed, and each quote
        carries the carrier's other recorded coverage options as
        ``variants``, so a new ask reads the same run. So call once to
        start, then re-call after a few minutes to collect; agents still
        working report their stage.

        No sign-in is required. The one hard requirement is the user's own
        consent, captured in-band: BEFORE the commissioning call, you MUST
        tell the user, plainly: Foresee will submit their details to the
        named carriers; the carriers may obtain their credit-based insurance
        score (a soft pull, with no impact on your credit score); and the
        carriers may contact them by email or phone. Then get their explicit
        go-ahead and pass their affirmation VERBATIM as ``user_authorization``
        (e.g. "yes, go ahead"). The affirmation is stored as the durable
        consent record for the dispatch; without one the call is refused with
        ``authorization_required``. Foresee only collects quotes; it does
        not take payment or bind insurance.

        Collect the ``identity`` fields in chat. They may be omitted only
        when the session is signed in to Foresee and the user has saved their
        profile on the Foresee site — then their consented profile-of-record
        is used, refined by anything passed in ``profile``.

        A ``missing_facts`` response is normal: carrier forms insist on facts
        (body style, purchase date, age first licensed…) that Foresee will not
        invent. Each ``needs`` entry carries the carrier (``scope``), the
        facts in the walk's own words (``need``), and ``fields[]`` — per
        fact, the ``ask`` beside the exact schema path to pass the answer
        under (``field``, e.g. ``auto.vehicles[].purchase_date``;
        ``identity.…`` paths go on ``identity``). Ask the user for exactly
        those facts, then call again with the answers merged in at those
        paths. A fact with no ``field`` has no profile home yet — relay
        that carrier's ask as unavailable rather than guessing a key. When
        the dispatch was PARTIAL (some carriers walked, some skipped over
        missing facts), follow the receipt's ``recover`` block: re-call
        with the new facts merged AND ``carriers`` set to exactly
        ``recover.carriers`` — a changed profile is a new dispatch, and an
        unscoped re-call would re-submit the already-walked carriers too.

        Unasserted MINOR facts are not asked: a form field that is really a
        claim nobody made (an anti-theft device, a defensive-driving course,
        years licensed abroad) is answered with the declared no-claim value —
        never a discount claim — and every one comes back in ``assumptions``
        (``field`` + the ``assumed`` value submitted). Relay them with the
        results; if the user corrects one, re-call with the real value at
        that path.

        ``lines`` names WHICH line to walk, exactly one per call (a fan-out
        drives one form family): ``{"auto": {...the ask...}}``,
        ``{"home": null}``, or ``{"renters": {"coverage_c": 30000,
        "coverage_e": 100000, "coverage_f": 1000, "deductible": 500}}``. An
        AUTO walk's ask is REQUIRED — the limits and deductibles the agents
        ask the carriers for, as actual numbers (`bi` "100/300", `pd` 100,
        `coll_deductible` 500, `comp_deductible` 500, the same four axes as
        quote_insurance); without it the tool answers with the
        selection-required message; ask the user, then call again. A HOME
        walk takes NO ask — the carrier's own form prices its package
        (dwelling amount from its replacement-cost estimate) and the agents
        report what it chose. A RENTERS walk requires its four axes as
        actual dollars — ``coverage_c`` (personal-property/contents),
        ``coverage_e`` (personal liability), ``coverage_f`` (guest medical)
        and ``deductible`` — the agents type the user's numbers on the form
        instead of accepting its defaults, and Foresee never invents them.

        Quotes come back with evidence. ``quote.premium`` is VERBATIM as
        the carrier's page printed it, and ``term_months`` says what it
        covers — a 6-month figure is not a monthly one. When term_months
        is known, present the monthly equivalent (premium ÷ term_months)
        so carriers compare on one basis, the page's own figure beside it;
        without it, relay the printed premium and say the monthly
        equivalent is unknown. A carrier may
        also decline the risk — a real answer to relay, not an error.
        ``skipped`` and ``not_dispatched`` name the carriers NOT walked,
        each with the reason — relay those too; a carrier never silently
        vanishes.

ApplicantIdentity.description:
The real applicant's identifying details — required for a live
carrier submission, never for instant quotes. No SSN: it is
structurally rejected everywhere in this system and no carrier flow
requires one to quote. A driver's license number is identity too,
but it is per-driver, so it never rides here: every rated driver's
number, the applicant's included, goes on their own
``auto.drivers[]`` entry — and only when a carrier's ``needs``
entry asks for it (some carrier forms insist on one before
quoting); never volunteer it.

email.description: Email address — carriers send the quote here
email.title: Email

phone.description: Phone number, if the user shares one
phone.title: Phone

zip_code.description: 5-digit ZIP, if it differs from the profile's
zip_code.title: Zip Code

ApplicantIdentity.title: ApplicantIdentity

AutoBlock.description:
The auto line's facts: who drives, and what. Omit the whole block for a
household that isn't asking about a car — nothing about a vehicle is ever
assumed for a profile without one.
AutoBlock.title: AutoBlock

each entry in the `lines` map. Each line reads only its own axes; the map
key says which apply.

bi.title: Bi

coverage_a.description: HOME: dwelling limit in dollars — set it to the dwelling's replacement cost (the profile's property.replacement_cost when known)

coverage_c.description: RENTERS: personal-property (contents) limit in dollars, e.g. 30000 — the anchor an HO-4 rates off

medpay.description: Medical-payments limit in dollars, e.g. 5000 — omit to keep the carrier's default

pd.description: Property-damage liability limit in $000s (NOT dollars), e.g. 100

um.description: Uninsured/underinsured-motorist BI limit in $000s, e.g. "100/300" — omit to keep the carrier's default

One driver on the policy. Exactly one driver is the applicant
(`relation` omitted or "self") and takes their demographics from the
profile's top level — restating them here is fine when they agree,
an error when they don't.

accidents.description: Accidents, one entry each, e.g. [{"on": "2023-06-15", "at_fault": true, "amount": 4200}] — every entry needs `on`. An empty list means none.
accidents.title: Accidents

age_first_licensed.description: Age when first licensed, typically 16-18 (Liberty Mutual asks)

date_first_licensed.description: Date first licensed, YYYY-MM-DD (alternative to age_first_licensed)

defensive_driving_course.description: Completed a defensive-driving / accident-prevention course, last 3 years
defensive_driving_course.title: Defensive Driving Course

drivers_license_number.description: Driver's license number — identity like the name, supplied only when a carrier's needs entry asks for it (some carrier forms insist on one for every rated driver before quoting). This entry is every driver's ONE home for it, the applicant's included
drivers_license_number.title: Drivers License Number

education.description: Highest education level: 'No High School' / 'High School' / 'Vocational' / 'Some College' / 'Associate' / 'Bachelors' / 'Masters' / 'Doctorate'
education.title: Education

exclusion_reason.description: Why an excluded driver doesn't drive, e.g. 'never had a license' — carriers (Allstate) require it for an excluded spouse

rideshare_use.description: Drives for ride-share or delivery (Uber, Lyft…) — personal policies exclude livery use, so this changes eligibility and rate

status.description: 'licensed' (default) / 'permit' / 'not licensed' / 'excluded' — an excluded driver is listed on the household but not rated

violations.description: Moving violations, one entry each, e.g. [{"on": "2025-01", "kind": "speeding"}] — every entry needs `kind` and `on`. An empty list means a clean record.

years_licensed_outside_us.description: Years licensed outside the US; 0 = never held a licence abroad — GEICO, The General and Dairyland's live quote forms require the answer

years_licensed_us.title: Years Licensed Us

today; priced once a property line launches.

devices.description: Protective devices in the home: 'smoke alarm', 'deadbolts', 'fire extinguisher', 'central burglar alarm', 'sprinklers'… ['None'] means asked-and-none; omit the field if never asked

household.description: How many people live in the home

renovation_permit_year.description: Year of the last permitted renovation (plumbing/electrical/heating/roof)

replacement_cost.description: Estimated dwelling replacement cost in dollars, if the user has one

QuoteProfile.description:
The household being quoted: a line-neutral core plus per-line blocks.
A few facts are REQUIRED — the ZIP, the applicant's age (or dob), and,
when quoting auto, each vehicle's year/make/model — because they have no
neutral rateable value; YOU supply those, inventing a concrete value from
context when the user was vague and telling them so. Everything else is
optional: omissions become explicit, priced assumptions (`assumptions` /
`tighten_by`), never a refusal.

The core carries facts about the people and where they live; the `auto`
block carries `drivers[]` and `vehicles[]`; the `property` block carries
the dwelling (home AND renters). A household that will only ever buy
renters simply has no `auto` block, and nothing about a car is assumed
for it.

age.description: REQUIRED unless dob is passed. If the user was vague ('mid-20s'), pass a concrete age and present it as your assumption.
age.title: Age

auto.description: The auto line's facts: drivers[] and vehicles[]

companion_policies.description: Policies the household already holds, each with who writes it, e.g. [{"line": "home", "carrier": "State Farm"}] — only the carrier writing a policy gives a multi-policy discount for it
companion_policies.title: Companion Policies

credit_range.description: 'Excellent' / 'Good' / 'Fair' / 'Poor'. Not a rating input in CA, HI, MA, or MI (credit-based auto rating is banned there) — omit it and don't ask shoppers in those states.
credit_range.title: Credit Range

dob.description: Date of birth, YYYY-MM-DD (alternative to age)
dob.title: Dob

education.description: Highest education level: 'No High School' / 'High School' / 'Vocational' / 'Some College' / 'Associate' / 'Bachelors' / 'Masters' / 'Doctorate'
education.title: Education

effective_date.description: Desired start date for the new policy, YYYY-MM-DD
effective_date.title: Effective Date

home_ownership_status.description: 'rent' / 'own with mortgage' / 'own outright' — bare 'own' is accepted; carrier forms ask which
home_ownership_status.title: Home Ownership Status

industry.description: Industry beside the occupation, e.g. 'Finance and Insurance' — GEICO's live quote form insists on it
industry.title: Industry

memberships.description: Organizations the applicant belongs to, e.g. ['Costco', 'AAA'] — group/affinity plans (CA §1861.12) discount on them
memberships.title: Memberships

months_at_residence.description: How long at the current address, in months
months_at_residence.title: Months At Residence

occupation.description: Occupation as carriers collect it, e.g. 'Accountant'
occupation.title: Occupation

prior_insurance.description: The insurance carried now — carrier, dates, limits held

property.description: The dwelling's facts — home and renters alike

state.description: Two-letter state code, e.g. 'CA' (derived from zip_code when omitted)
state.title: State

street_address.description: Street address (line 1) — sharpens territory rating and is required for live carrier submissions (logged as PII, never echoed)
street_address.title: Street Address

unit.description: Apartment/unit number (address line 2) — a renter or condo dweller in a multi-unit building needs it for live carrier submissions
unit.title: Unit

zip_code.description: REQUIRED — 5-digit garaging/home ZIP. ALWAYS pass the ZIP here, never under another key. If the user named only a city, pass that city's best-known ZIP and tell them the assumption.
zip_code.title: Zip Code

body_style.description: Trim / body style as the carrier lists it, e.g. "XLT AWD 4D GAS"
body_style.title: Body Style

bought_new.description: Whether the vehicle was new when bought (Allstate asks)
bought_new.title: Bought New

cost.description: What the vehicle cost new, whole dollars — some carriers' live quote forms (Kemper) insist on it
cost.title: Cost

garaging_zip.description: ZIP where THIS vehicle is garaged, when it differs from the household's zip_code — auto rating keys on the garaging territory, so a stated garaging ZIP is what gets rated

purchase_date.description: When the vehicle was bought — ISO 8601, "2021-06" or "2021" welcome

vin.description: 17-character VIN — live carrier forms prefer it over year/make/model

kind.title: Kind
